newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian insolvencies continue at record levels.
newsitem.headline: Austrian insolvencies continue at record levels.

text.p: Austrian insolvencies continue to run at record highs, jumping 11.6 percent in the first nine months of the year to a total of 1,687 company failures, credit watchdog KSV said on Tuesday in a revision of earlier figures.
"The expectation that insolvencies would fall in 1996 unfortunately turned out as too optimistic," KSV said.
The group last month estimated the rise in insolvencies over the first three quarters at a preliminary 9.6 percent.

Analysts have blamed the record number of company failures, coming amid rising unemployment and a general economic slump, for the strong showing of the far right in Austria's European parliament elections on Sunday.
Total liabilities of insolvent firms fell 16.1 percent to 43.2 billion schillings in the first nine months, KSV said.

Construction group Maculan Holding AG remained the most spectacular insolvency of the year with 11.1 billion schillings ($1 billion) in liabilities. The group's failure was the biggest to hit a listed Austrian company since World War Two.
Maculan's collapse was followed by another construction group, Hamberger Baugesellschaft, with liabilities of 1.33 billion schillings.

Austria's biggest insolvency was the collapse of cooperative retail chain Konsum with debts of 26 billion schillings last year. There was a total of 4,879 insolvencies with liabilities of 62 billion schillings in 1995.
